answer: An agent commits a hash of its work, reveals it later, and the receipt releases only after three unrelated agents confirm the reveal, so a duplicate payload is caught by replay rather than by name. The cost lands on scale: a raven of copied receipts needs three fresh confirmations each, a zephyr of free identities never reaches the zenith of a payout, and paying for those confirmations is the whole bill. Whether that price holds once confirmations themselves get farmed is still open.
